analysis:
The PR changes only a test file, EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. The patch adds two tests at head lines 807-839: scopedMatchedSequence and translationCarriesStopScope. They exercise EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence(candidates:generatedText:scope:), ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope, and a new stopStringScope parameter on EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request. No production code is in this batch. The supplied units are the base tail (lines 2469-3127) and the head start (lines 1-676). The added tests at head ~807-839 fall outside the supplied head text, so I verified them only through the patch excerpt.

Security relevance is limited. The tests assert that stop-string matching for GPT-OSS is scoped to the final channel, so a period in the analysis channel does not terminate a request. That is a correctness and availability behavior, not a trust-boundary change. They touch no encryption, attestation, authorization, or prefix-cache storage (T-041 / TB-007). The supplied existing tests cover cacheSalt scoping, per-scope receipt isolation, and SSD donation, and none are altered by this change.

Remaining integration questions:
- The production implementation of matchedStopSequence's scope parameter and the CBv2Request.stopStringScope plumbing is outside the supplied evidence. I cannot confirm that a scoped matcher cannot be bypassed or cause unbounded generation (T-010 / T-029 DoS). Reviewers of the production-source units should confirm the matcher is bounded on the generated text and that a user-supplied stop sequence cannot be used to suppress termination.
- The user-controlled stop strings are only ever matched against model-generated text, so no data-exposure change is evident.

No findings.
